analysis:
Examined all supplied patches, source and mode metadata against the canonical index and selected details. No independently supported security regression was established in this scope. ServingReadiness.swift:31–74 adds state-derived diagnostics: disconnected/untrusted/offline states block, absent status has a 90-second grace period, and App Attest authorization delegates currency checking to hasCurrentAppAttestAuthorization. Lines 54–64 label hardware trust without an authorization object and the legacy path as authorized. Integration must verify these labels match the consumed coordinator contract, rather than implying serving permission from a legacy label (A-016, TB-011, T-052, T-058), and that trust snapshots are cleared or rebound on reconnection (T-053). Neither the predicate implementation, snapshot lifecycle nor callers are supplied; no bypass is proven.
ProviderLogger.swift:147–149 adds only fixed operational messages. Existing public/private overloads and redaction remain unchanged; these additions expose no prompts, tokens, keys, receipts or stable identities (A-001, A-008, T-058). ServingReadiness.swift:78–160 formats recovery advice without executing it or changing credentials or attestation policy.
ProviderLoop+Capacity.swift head:82 invokes superviseServingAuthorization after existing asynchronous capacity/model refresh work. Its implementation is absent and is a material integration dependency: examine reconnect/re-registration triggers, rate limits, idle/in-flight guards, connection invalidation and authorization expiry handling for T-053/T-057 and availability effects. The new log vocabulary alone does not prove recovery behavior. Supplied changes do not alter encryption, billing, native inference admission, fan authority or T-041 cache controls; this is not coverage of their unchanged implementations.
